title: Commercial intake protocol for pricing exceptions, marketplace credits, and allocation transparency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Create a pragmatic, auditable intake and prioritization protocol for non-bug commercial requests related to pricing exceptions, commitment invoices, marketplace credits, and cost-allocation asks from enterprise customers. Goal is to reduce churn and time-to-resolution while ensuring consistent cost accounting and guardrails for revenue retention.

Scope: Requests handled by this protocol include: commitment credit applications, invoice adjustments or one-off credits, marketplace revenue sharing disputes and offsets, cross-team cost allocation requests for customer-facing discounts, and bespoke pricing exceptions for strategic accounts. Excluded: core billing platform bugs, payment failures, or legal contract negotiations (those route directly to Finance/Legal).

Deliverables:
- A lightweight intake form (required fields listed below).
- A 4-step triage rubric to score and route requests.
- SLA tiers and escalation path.
- Decision templates for common outcomes (approve, partial credit, deny, escalate to sales/legal).
- Audit log schema for Finance and Revenue Ops.

Required intake fields: Requestor name, requestor role, customer name & orgID, commitment/contract ID (if applicable), invoice number(s), requested outcome (credit amount or redistribution), business justification (quantified if possible), ARR impact estimate, supporting artifacts (PO, email thread, contract clause: quote), urgency and downstream downtime/impact, proposed approver (if pre-negotiated).

Triage rubric (score 0-10 across factors):
- Contractual obligation (0-3): explicit clause = 3, ambiguous = 1, none = 0.
- Financial magnitude (0-3): >$50k = 3, $10k-50k = 2, <$10k = 1, immaterial = 0.
- Strategic signal (0-2): strategic customer or expansion motion = 2, standard =1, not strategic =0.
- Operational risk & compliance (0-2): regulatory or audit requirement =2, billing error =1, no risk =0.
Total score thresholds: 8-10 -> Rapid Approve lane (Finance + PM signoff within 48h). 5-7 -> Review lane (Finance + Revenue Ops with PM decision within 7 days). 0-4 -> Standard lane (PR for denial or small credit; respond within 14 days).

Routing rules:
- If Contractual obligation score ==3: autoprioritize to Finance for immediate reconciliation.
- If Financial magnitude >=3 and Strategic signal >=1: require Sales/AE endorsement + VP Commercial approval.
- If Marketplace dispute: auto-associate to Marketplace team and Revenue Ops; escrow credits and create ticket in Marketplace backlog.

SLA & escalation:
- Acknowledgement within 24 business hours.
- Target resolution windows as above by lane.
- If unresolved by SLA boundary, auto-escalate to Director of Revenue Ops and the assigned PM.

Audit & recordkeeping:
- Every approved adjustment requires: approval chain (email or Linear signoff), GL impact entry id, customer-facing note for invoice, and a follow-up reconciliation in next month’s billing cycle.

Decision templates (summary):
- Approve full credit: include amount, GL codes, expected invoice adjustment date, notes for customer, and internal reason.
- Approve partial: same as above with rationale for partial amount and next steps for collection.
- Deny: cite contract clause or lack of justification; suggest alternative (discount on renewal or one-off waiver subject to Sales approval).
- Escalate: clear escalation reason and required artifacts (legal review, SLA evidence, exec signoff).

Metrics to track (KPIs):
- Time to acknowledgement (hours).
- Time to resolution by lane (days).
- Percent of approved vs denied adjustments.
- ARR impact of adjustments (monthly).
- Post-adjustment retention delta at 90 days.

Integration points & artifacts:
- Confluence: canonical playbook doc link (placeholder: https://confluence.redwood.ai/commercial-intake-playbook).
- Finance GL mapping sheet: Google Drive link (placeholder).
- Templates: email response templates and Linear workflow that auto-tags tickets: pricing-intake, finance-review, marketplace.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Tight SLAs reduce revenue leakage but may increase accidental credits; mitigations include checklist and mandatory evidence attachments.
- Heavily manual approvals scale poorly; plan to instrument scoring and auto-routing in Phase 2.

Phase plan:
- Phase 0 (this ticket): finalize intake form, rubric, templates, and run tabletop with Finance/Revenue Ops/Sales (2 weeks).
- Phase 1: implement Linear intake template + auto-tagging and dashboards (4 weeks).
- Phase 2: automate scoring and partial approvals for <$10k credits; integrate with billing system (Q2 2026).

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form published in Confluence and Linear template created.
- Two tabletop runs documented with signoffs from Finance, RevOps, Sales.
- Dashboard showing first 30-day metrics for intake volume and SLA compliance.

Next steps:
1) PM to circulate draft intake form to Finance/RevOps by 2026-02-27.
2) Schedule tabletop on 2026-03-03.
3) Update Linear template and assign automation tickets for Phase 1 engineering work.
